history.content: Hi, my phone has no service at all—no bars, nothing loads, and I can't send picture messages. Can you help?

I can help you troubleshoot your phone’s service and picture messaging issues. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, customer ID, or your full name and date of birth?
Sure, my name is Sofia Martinez and my phone number is +1-617-555-0148.

Thank you for providing your information. To help resolve your "no service" and picture messaging issues, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks on your phone.

First, could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know what icons or messages you see at the top of your screen? This will help determine if Airplane Mode is on, if there’s a SIM issue, or if there’s another problem affecting your service.
At the top of my screen I see the Airplane Mode icon, a 'No Signal' icon, 'Data Enabled', and my battery percentage. It looks like Airplane Mode might be on.

It appears that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone, which disables all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data. This is likely the reason you have no service and cannot send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your device. Once you do, check if your service returns (you should see signal bars appear) and let me know if you’re able to send picture messages again. If the issue persists after turning off Airplane Mode, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting.
Airplane mode is now off. I see a few signal bars, but the signal is still very weak and I still can't send picture messages.

Thank you for updating me. Since you now have some signal but it’s weak and you still can’t send picture messages, let’s continue troubleshooting:

1. Could you confirm if you see “4G,” “LTE,” “5G,” or any network type indicator in your status bar?
2. Are you able to use mobile data for browsing the internet or using apps, or is that not working as well?
3. Do you see any error messages when trying to send a picture message (MMS)?

Your answers will help me pinpoint the next steps to resolve your service and MMS issues.

I don't see 4G, LTE, or 5G in the status bar—just a couple of weak signal bars. Mobile data isn't working; nothing loads. When I try to send a picture message, it just fails to send without any specific error message.

Thank you for the details. Since you have weak signal, no network type indicator (like 4G/5G), and mobile data isn’t working, let’s check for possible SIM card or network configuration issues.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone and let me know if it shows as active, missing, or locked. This will help determine if your phone is recognizing the SIM card correctly.
My SIM card status shows as active and detected by the phone.

Thank you for confirming your SIM card is active and detected. Since the SIM is working but you still have weak signal, no network type indicator, and no mobile data, the next step is to check your phone’s network mode preference. Sometimes, if your phone is set to use only older networks (like 2G/3G), it can cause weak signal and prevent mobile data and MMS from working.

Could you please check your phone’s network mode preference and let me know what it is currently set to (e.g., 2G, 3G, 4G, 5G, or automatic)?
My network mode is set to '4G/5G preferred.'

Thank you for checking. Since your network mode is set correctly and your SIM is active, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can cause issues with both mobile data and MMS (picture messaging).

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if anything appears incorrect or if the MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL is missing? If you’re unsure, just let me know what you see for the APN name and MMSC URL.
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is 'fast.telecom.net', but it says 'Not set' and the MMSC URL is 'http://mms.telecom.net/mms/wapenc'.

Thank you for providing your APN details. The APN name showing as "Not set" could be causing your mobile data and MMS issues, even though the MMSC URL appears correct.

To fix this, please reset your APN settings to the default values on your phone. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Once you’ve done this, let me know if your service and picture messaging start working, or if you still experience issues.

I've already reset the APN settings to default and rebooted my phone. The APN is now set to 'internet' with the MMSC URL 'http://mms.carrier.com/mms'. After rebooting, the signal is still weak, and I still can't send picture messages.

Thank you for resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone. Since the APN and MMSC are now set to default values, but you still have weak signal and cannot send picture messages, let’s check a few more things:

1. Are you currently indoors or in an area where signal is usually weak? If possible, try moving to a different location (near a window or outside) to see if the signal improves.
2. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your device? Sometimes, Wi-Fi Calling can interfere with MMS. If it is enabled, please try turning it off and then attempt to send a picture message again.

Let me know the results after trying these steps. If the issue persists, we can continue troubleshooting.
I'm at home in Boston, where I usually have good signal. I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is not enabled. The signal and picture messaging still aren't working.

Your line was suspended, which explains why you had weak or no signal and could not send picture messages. I have now resumed your line, and it is active again.

Please reboot your phone to restore full service. After rebooting, you should see your signal return to normal and be able to use mobile data and send picture messages.

Let me know if everything works after the reboot or if you need further assistance.

response.result: Line LN-8830142 has been resumed and is now Active.

history.content: I rebooted my phone as you asked. Now the signal bars are full, it shows 5G, and I was able to send a picture message successfully. Everything is working perfectly now!

That’s great news! I’m glad your service and picture messaging are working perfectly now.

If you have any other questions or need further assistance in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a wonderful day!
